podcast: From Founder to Leader: Human stories behind bio + climate tech startups

0c0adf489d.q: How does Homeworld Collective use AI to automate grant-making workflows with a tiny team?
0c0adf489d.a: Homeworld Collective wired Claude with email history and standard operating procedures from Notion to create eight daily automated triggers that scan for grant extension requests and automatically draft responses when information is insufficient. When applicants provide the needed information, the system automatically drafts a contract and sends it through PandaDoc, with Paul reviewing and manually approving each draft before sending.
0c0adf489d.rq: What do you wish you had someone to do? And then just throw in a prompt, like, can you do this?
ks: Homeworld Collective has three full-time team members
Homeworld Collective was founded in 2019 and went into 2022 under co-founders Daniel Goodwin and Paul Reginato
GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 were released when Paul's career pivot to climate technology happened, around February 2023
Paul has used Claude AI for approximately three and a half years as of this recording
Claude Opus 5.5 costs $20 per month or $100 per month subscription plan

766b450827.q: What is the Jadgen frontier concept and how does it apply to using AI in startup operations?
766b450827.a: The Jadgen frontier, possibly coined by Ethan Mollick, describes the fact that AI is constantly changing and the frontier of what is available constantly shifts, bumping up against the frontier of what you know how to do and what you need to do. Part of working with AI is just doing it, and sometimes there are inefficiencies and sometimes there are great efficiencies, requiring constant learning about how your own context relates to an ever-shifting AI landscape.

6449ac966a.q: Why is AI ineffective at creating strategic documents from scratch and what is the dark side of AI-generated strategic content?
6449ac966a.a: AI is trained on the past so it cannot create the future; human cognition is the creator of the future and should use AI to weave together past context. When AI generates strategic content, it produces material that is just right enough to feel correct but wrong enough to be exhausting to fix, creating an uncanny valley effect where readers' brains turn off and assume it is true when it is actually wrong. People increasingly detect AI-generated copy, and there is cognitive decline risk when humans surrender their own effort and thinking to AI.

b5e06f54fc.q: How did Paul Himmelstein use Claude to update Homeworld Collective's strategic plan without letting AI write it from scratch?
b5e06f54fc.a: Paul took Claude (which had eight months of organizational context) and had it compare transcripts from five presentations of a new pitch deck against the existing 11-page strategic plan, noting all inconsistencies. Using the new Google Docs connector, Claude made only suggested changes and added comments wherever discrepancies existed, allowing Paul to review approximately 40 comments and multiple suggested edits in a few hours rather than spending far longer updating manually.
